clue.text: They say outstanding elite oil job has been arranged for oldie

indicators.note: they say signals that a word is to be heard spoken rather than read, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a debt still outstanding is one owed

indicators.note: has been arranged tells us the letters of the phrase before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has fixed up an oily job for an elite who is past it, and they are said to be very good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' turns OWED (outstanding, as a debt) into ODE. 'has been arranged' rearranges ELITE OIL JOB into TO BILLIE JOE. This is the 1967 Bobbie Gentry hit, which sets up the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old popular song, and this 1967 hit counts as one now.

clue.text: My mistake, removing covers of book — note added

indicators.note: removing covers of says the outer letters of the word book are taken off, keeping its inside

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A writer admits an error: they stripped the covers from a book and added a note.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation said on making a slip, the same thing as admitting an error.

clue.text: God's section of the rosary?

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of the rosary prayers might be thought to belong to God.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', so 'God's' means 'God is', a phrase that can stand in for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Conservative group initially opposing local democratic government as no good

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the first letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Traditionalists object to local democratic councils, saying they are no good.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the long-standing, tradition-minded members of a group who resist change.

clue.text: See 1
Lawyers supported by cathedral city? Only just

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported by means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: barristers as a body are called the Bar
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: Do the lawyers have a cathedral city backing them? Only just.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the piece 'supported by' another sits above it. Ely is a small cathedral city near Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something done by the narrowest margin was scarcely managed.

clue.text: Porky about fine husband, getting on, in relation to rights ending on death

definitions.text: in relation to rights ending on death

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the next one

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: pork pie means lie, shortened to porky
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
getting on in years means old

explanation.surface: A lie about a fine and a husband getting on, perhaps in a dispute over an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky' is British slang for a lie: it comes from the rhyme pork pie = lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes property held only for the holder's lifetime, so the tenure stops when they die.

clue.text: Foolish, I had at beginning interrupted referring to listener?

parts.note: I had shortens to I'd

indicators.note: at beginning picks the opening letter of the word interrupted

parts.note: otic means relating to the ear, the part that listens

explanation.surface: A foolish person admits they interrupted from the start, and wonders whether they were addressing the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted' looks like an insertion signal, but 'at beginning' only takes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple synonym: both mean senseless or stupid.

clue.text: Jack referring to a hotel, source of bad luck

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
on means about or concerning
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Jack talks about a hotel that brings bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: From the biblical prophet thrown overboard, a person thought to bring misfortune on those around them.

clue.text: Guarantee does not have right result

indicators.note: does not have means a letter is taken out of the word for guarantee

parts.note: to ensure something is to guarantee it

explanation.surface: A guarantee doesn't give the right outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' is the verb here, to follow as a consequence, not the noun it seems to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym used as a verb: to follow on as a consequence.

clue.text: Slow worker's place, more bizarre

parts.note: PL is the street-name abbreviation for Place
odder means stranger, more bizarre

explanation.surface: A slow worker's workplace is even stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who toils on doggedly but without speed or flair.

clue.text: Twenty-four hour period concludes for Allies

parts.note: a day, here Friday, shortened to Fri
ends means concludes

explanation.surface: A day-long period finishes for the Allied powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allies' hints at the Second World War Allies, but here it is just people on your side.
explanation.definitionFit: Close companions are those who stand on your side.

clue.text: In stall, a hatch, I examine Mississippi flower

indicators.note: In says the answer is sitting inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone examines a stall and a hatch, looking for a flower from Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword shorthand for a river (something that flows). The Tallahatchie Bridge is where the theme song's events take place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tallahatchie is a river in the US state of Mississippi, and a river is a thing that flows.

clue.text: A teaching expert in retirement?

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree, held by a trained teacher

explanation.surface: Is this a retired teacher?
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' here means going to bed, not giving up work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired for the night is lying in bed.

clue.text: Face being laid up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word laid is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A face being laid up, as if someone were ill in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a clock or watch is its dial.

clue.text: Game reduced in length as there's no publicity about it?

indicators.note: as there's no means the following piece is taken out
about it says the removed piece sits around the rest, at either end

parts.note: a text cut short is abridged
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A game gets cut short because nobody is promoting it.
explanation.walkthrough: A and D sit at either end of ABRIDGED, wrapped round the rest, which is why the clue says 'about it'. The answer also echoes the theme's Tallahatchie Bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in two partnerships.

clue.text: Musician might use this cut, perm, learner restyled

indicators.note: restyled, as a hairdresser restyles hair, means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A trainee hairdresser restyles a cut and perm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restyled' rearranges CUT, PERM and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A plectrum is the small pick a guitarist strums or plucks strings with.

clue.text: Referring to the Spanish dance

parts.note: re means about or concerning
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A note about the Spanish dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish dance' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'dance'. The reel is Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.

clue.text: Nearly all Medical Officers on time

parts.note: MO is the abbreviation for Medical Officer, plural MOs

explanation.surface: Almost all the doctors turned up on time.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulk or greater part of something, which is close to all of it.

clue.text: Inn Luigi converted providing pasta

indicators.note: converted means the letters of the words before it are made into something new

explanation.surface: Luigi converts his inn into an Italian restaurant serving pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguine is a type of flat, narrow ribbon pasta.

clue.text: Mail a tad unreliable in coastal region?

indicators.note: unreliable suggests the letters of the phrase before it cannot be trusted to stay in place

explanation.surface: The post is a bit unreliable in some seaside area.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatia is the historic coastal region of Croatia on the Adriatic.

clue.text: In lively manner, I'm entering top grade international organisation

parts.note: A is the top mark or grade

indicators.note: entering means the first piece goes into the second

parts.note: NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization
I'm shortened is IM

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of joining a top-ranked international body.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning a passage should be played with spirit and animation.

clue.text: Sweet when welcoming paper associated with monarch

indicators.note: welcoming means the first word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: associated with puts the two pieces side by side

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A sweet moment when a newspaper is linked with the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afters' is the British informal word for the dessert course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the pudding course after the main dish is called afters.

clue.text: Zeal of group pinching diesel oil after Duke's left

indicators.note: pinching means the first piece holds the second inside

parts.note: a group of four, such as a quartet

indicators.note: left means the duke's letter has gone away

parts.note: DERV is the British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles

explanation.surface: A gang steals fuel oil once the Duke has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British trade name for diesel used in road vehicles. 'Duke' is not a person in the story, only a letter to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe intense passion or enthusiasm for something.

clue.text: Performs in play in street — stick around!

indicators.note: around means the pieces are turned round and read the other way

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: Street actors are told to stick around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play in street' tempts you to put ACT inside ST, but 'in play' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out a role or a scene on stage is to perform it.

clue.text: Policeman reportedly linked with upper class singer

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: bobby is British slang for a police officer
the gentry are the well-born class just below the nobility

explanation.surface: A police officer, people say, has links to a posh singer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bobby' is a British police officer. Bobbie Gentry wrote and sang Ode to Billie Joe.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobbie Gentry is the American who wrote and performed the 1967 song at the heart of this puzzle.

clue.text: Anger about book — authoritative one?

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: bile means bad temper or anger

explanation.surface: Is a book that provokes anger an authoritative one?
explanation.definitionFit: Any work regarded as the definitive reference on a subject is called its bible.

clue.text: Instrument to prohibit judo in extreme instances?

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit

indicators.note: in extreme instances points to the outermost letters of the word judo

explanation.surface: An instrument used to forbid judo in the worst cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed musical instrument with a round drum-like body.

clue.text: Boss's examination curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a study is a close examination

explanation.surface: The boss's inspection was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is a raised knob or stud, not a manager; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob, the same thing as a stud on a surface.

clue.text: Over-sentimental TV where odd characters feature

indicators.note: odd characters means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the words

explanation.surface: Mawkish television where eccentric characters appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A British word for something sweetly cute or cloying to the point of being sickly.

clue.text: Began badly rejecting the Italian language

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the word began are jumbled
rejecting means the Italian word is sent back the other way

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Someone started badly by turning down the Italian language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Began' looks like the verb of the surface sentence, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

clue.text: Native American food captivating act on tour

indicators.note: captivating means holding the next piece captive inside

parts.note: chow is slang for food

indicators.note: on tour suggests the word act wandering about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A travelling show is enchanted by the food served on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tour' signals an anagram, not travel; 'captivating' is the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are a Native American people originally of the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Financial aspects of refusal splitting English entertainers

indicators.note: splitting means the refusal goes inside, dividing the other pieces

parts.note: comics are comedians, who entertain
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Some English comedians are divided by their refusal to talk about money.
explanation.definitionFit: The financial side of a venture, as in the economics of a scheme, means its costs and returns.

clue.text: Trip around good raised area

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: A walk around a nice hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow stretch of elevated ground.
